mutations.because: K-D9's only refusal is a duplicate t on one track's same clock. Weakening the strict inequality from `<=` to `<` still catches a stop out of order (descending), but lets two stops at the exact same t through — the composition question K-D9 answers (two tracks may share a property) would then be silently true within one track too.

orderedKeys appends unnamed keys at the end, so dropping tracks from LAYER_KEY_ORDER does not make it disappear — it falls into the same tail bucket as any other unrecognised key, which a plain 'tracks appears in the output' assertion cannot tell apart from tracks sitting at its declared sixth position. Only a fixture with an unnamed key written before tracks in source order proves the position.
